title: Every woven []byte->string assignment/declaration/return heap-allocates, even with IAST disabled or sampled out
claim: BytesToString is not inlinable in customer packages (shape cost 131 > 80), so `result := string(value)` escapes (operators.go:199:19 'escapes to heap'). Plain Go keeps a non-escaping `s := string(b)` of <=32 bytes on the stack. Weaving therefore adds one heap allocation per wrapped conversion on every execution, independent of sampling/activity (identical counts inactive and active-untainted). README:31 calls these conversions 'allocation-preserving', which is false for non-escaping results. Measured 0 -> 1 allocs/op (ConvLocal, StringSliceLocal). A prototype using a non-generic inlinable gate helper plus a template emitting BytesToStringValue([]byte(x)) restores 0 allocs/op.
repro_command: cd <copy> && GOTOOLCHAIN=go1.26.6 go test -run '^$' -bench . -benchtime=20000x ./perfsample  vs  go tool orchestrion go test -run '^$' -bench . -benchtime=20000x ./perfsample (sample.go/sample_test.go/extra_test.go in evidence dir)

title: Operator fast gate HasValues is never inlined into generic wrappers in customer builds, and ConcatN zero-alloc behavior depends on that accident
claim: When a customer package instantiates iast/propagation generics without importing internal/taint/operatorbridge (always true for customers), the Go inliner does not inline operatorbridge.HasValues into the instantiated shape bodies (reproduced with plain go build on go1.26.6 and go1.27.0). Every woven concat/slice/conversion therefore pays extra out-of-line calls before the cheap gate. The inlinability of Concat2/Concat3 depends on it: with HasValues inlinable (blank import), concat2Result/concat3Result drop to cost 79/80, get inlined, and Concat2/Concat3 exceed budget (91/94). Their results then escape, and 2-3 operand local concats go from 0 to 1 allocs/op (ConcatConvOperand 1 -> 2).
repro_command: compile a package that calls iastprop.Concat2/BytesToString with and without `_ "github.com/DataDog/dd-iast-go/internal/taint/operatorbridge"` using -gcflags=-m=2 (see evidence file)

title: copy() into the local inputs array makes every concat/Join operand leak to the heap
claim: joinStringHit/joinBytesHit copy elements into a fixed local array with copy(), which escape analysis models as flowing element contents to the heap ('leaking param content: elements'). Through internal.ConcatN/JoinString, every operand of a woven `+` chain and strings.Join leaks. The compiler-optimized zero-copy `string(b) + "x"` (deliberately left unwrapped by the design) therefore becomes a real heap string: ConcatConvOperand goes from 0 to 1 allocs/op. Replacing copy with an explicit element loop gives 'elements does not escape' and restores 0 allocs/op (prototype v2/v3).
repro_command: see bench-plain.txt vs bench-woven.txt (ConcatConvOperand) and bench-woven-prototype-v3.txt

title: Concat wrappers for 8-16 operands are not inlinable, so their non-escaping results always heap-allocate
claim: Concat8..Concat16 shape functions cost 81..97 (> 80), so `a+...+h` is computed inside an out-of-line function and escapes. Plain Go stack-allocates a non-escaping <=32-byte concat result. Measured 0 -> 1 allocs/op (ConcatLocal8, ConcatLocal16), unconditionally. Arity 2-7 is currently inlined (see F2 for its fragility).

title: Non-inlinable wrappers force fresh results that plain code keeps on the stack to escape (Buffer.String, strconv.Quote*)
claim: Natively inlinable calls whose fresh result does not escape in plain code (bytes.Buffer.String, strconv.Quote/QuoteToASCII/QuoteToGraphic, strings.Clone) are replaced by non-inlinable wrappers (cost 98-220), so the result escapes: BufferStringLocal 0 -> 1, QuoteLocal 1 -> 2 allocs/op, regardless of IAST state.
repro_command: compare BufferStringLocal/QuoteLocal in bench-plain.txt vs bench-woven.txt

title: Writer receiver escape is unconditional and always happens; README says it 'can' happen
claim: Any local strings.Builder/bytes.Buffer with at least one wrapped method call is moved to heap in every woven build ('moved to heap: sb/buf'), independent of IAST enablement, sampling, or taint: +1 alloc (+32 B Builder, +48 B Buffer) per writer. This is a documented and accepted trade-off. The wording understates its universality and does not quantify it.
repro_command: compare BuilderLocal/BufferLocal in bench-plain.txt vs bench-woven.txt

title: No named-call wrapper is inlinable and none has an inlinable pre-gate
claim: All ~75 strings/bytes/fmt/url/strconv wrappers exceed the inline budget (98-220), and writer Buffer wrappers use defer ('unhandled op DEFER'). Natively inlined calls such as strings.Cut, CutPrefix, TrimPrefix, and Builder.WriteString/String become at least two out-of-line calls (the wrapper, then internal.StringWindow at cost 268, which only then checks ActiveStore) even with IAST disabled. Unlike the operators, there is no call-site gate. No extra allocations were measured (CutLocal/TrimLocal 0).

location: orchestrion@23afa71d6dcb (toolexec compile-flag handling; child builds reuse parent flags at internal/jobserver/pkgs/resolve.go:197-224)
title: Woven builds reject -gcflags=-m=2
claim: `go tool orchestrion go build -gcflags='-m=2'` fails with 'invalid boolean value "2" for -m' (first seen while resolving the woven dependency iobridge, and later on the target package itself), while plain go build with the same compiler accepts it. `-m -m` or package-scoped gcflags work. This complicates escape/inlining audits of woven code.
